title: Trump Magazine Ceases Publication After 18 Months
description_short: Trump Magazine Ceases Publication After 18 Months
description_medium: TIME reports that Donald Trump launched an eponymous lifestyle magazine in 2007 for an affluent readership, and that it ceased publication about a year and a half later. The supplied source does not explain the magazine’s circulation, finances or reason for closing, so the shutdown cannot be attributed to a specific business failure.
description_long: TIME describes an attempt by Trump to extend his brand into publishing. The magazine launched in 2007 and was marketed as a glossy publication for affluent readers. A press release said it would reflect that audience’s interests through a broad cultural mix. About eighteen months after launch, the magazine ceased publication. The linked article places the title among Trump’s business failures but does not give circulation figures, advertising revenue, operating costs, the size of its staff or a reason for its closure. The available facts establish the launch and relatively short publication run, not why it ended or whether it lost money. A fuller account would need contemporaneous reporting about readership and the company’s decision to stop publishing. The short life of the magazine can be stated plainly without claiming that promotional hype caused its closure or that the venture had a particular financial outcome.
notes: Needs context: TIME supports the magazine’s 2007 launch and closure about eighteen months later but does not report circulation, finances or why publication ended.
Proposed correction: Keep the entry to the launch and closure unless contemporaneous business reporting documents the cause or financial result.
Removed the unsupported claim that the closure proved a gap between promotion and sustainable readership.

title: New York AG Secures Court Order: Trump to Pay $2 Million for Misuse of Trump Foundation Funds
description_short: New York AG Secures Court Order: Trump to Pay $2 Million for Misuse of Trump Foundation Funds
description_medium: On November 7, 2019, a New York court ordered Donald Trump to pay $2 million in damages for using charitable assets to intervene in the 2016 presidential primaries. Trump admitted to personally misusing Foundation funds and agreed to restrictions on future charitable service. The Trump Foundation had been dissolved under court supervision in December 2018; the stored entry date of January 28, 2016 instead refers to a separate Iowa fundraiser.
description_long: New York Attorney General Letitia James announced on November 7, 2019, that a state court had ordered Donald Trump to pay $2 million in damages for using Trump Foundation funds to influence the 2016 presidential primaries. Trump admitted to personally misusing charitable assets and agreed to restrictions on future charitable service. The Foundation had already been dissolved under court supervision in December 2018, with remaining assets distributed to charities. The case concerned a January 2016 Iowa fundraiser held while Trump skipped a Republican debate; the event raised about $2.8 million for the Foundation, according to the supplied correction record. That fundraiser and the later court order are related but distinct events nearly four years apart. The existing entry is dated January 28, 2016, while its title describes the 2019 judgment. This lane cannot change the stored date or split the fundraiser into its own entry, so the corrected account still requires a metadata update before it can be applied without leaving a date mismatch.
subcategory: Trump Foundation misuse and court order
notes: Needs context: The correction packet confirms the 2019 order, December 2018 dissolution, admissions and 2016 fundraiser, but the stored entry date is still January 28, 2016 while the title and description focus on the later judgment.

Proposed correction: Update the record date to November 7, 2019 for the court-order entry and create a separate January 28, 2016 entry for the fundraiser, or otherwise resolve the date/title mismatch before applying this description.

title: Trump Raises .1 Million Exploiting Criminal Mugshot
description_short: Trump campaign mugshot fundraising total is unclear in the supplied record
description_medium: The supplied record says Trump’s campaign sold merchandise featuring his Fulton County booking photo after his August 2023 arrest, but the reported donation amount is rendered only as “.1 million,” with the leading figure missing. The linked New York Times article predates the mugshot and returned HTTP 403, so it cannot establish the campaign total or merchandise details.
description_long: The entry concerns Donald Trump’s August 24, 2023 booking in Fulton County and the campaign’s use of his mugshot on merchandise and social media. The supplied summary says donations rose within a day and that the campaign offered shirts and mugs featuring the booking photo, but the amount appears as “.1 million,” without a leading digit. That figure cannot be responsibly reconstructed from the text. The linked New York Times article is dated August 14, before the booking and mugshot, and returned HTTP 403 when checked; it therefore does not support the fundraising amount or the campaign’s later merchandise sales. The record documents a claimed fundraising response to the image but does not establish the total, how much came from merchandise rather than donations, or the campaign’s revenue from sales. An accessible article dated after the booking or campaign financial records are needed before the title’s amount or its characterization of the fundraising can be completed.
notes: Needs context: The amount is corrupted as “.1 million,” and the linked August 14 NYT story predates the August 24 booking; it returned HTTP 403 and does not support the claimed total or merchandise sales.
Proposed correction: Replace the linked source with an accessible report or campaign records from after the booking, and supply the full fundraising figure before restoring an amount to the title.
Replaced the unsupported populated medium description and short card text; the missing amount was not inferred.

title: Trump Posts Dozens of Attacks on Prosecutors, Witnesses, and Judges
description_short: Trump Posts Dozens of Attacks on Prosecutors, Witnesses, and Judges
description_medium: The supplied account says Donald Trump used Truth Social in 2023 to attack special counsel Jack Smith, judges and witnesses in his criminal cases, prompting Smith to seek limits on Trump’s public statements because of witness-intimidation concerns. The linked Washington Post article timed out, so the individual posts and the court’s rulings on the requested restrictions could not be checked.
description_long: The supplied chronology describes repeated Truth Social posts by Donald Trump in 2023 attacking special counsel Jack Smith, judges overseeing his cases and witnesses by name. It says Smith sought protective restrictions on Trump’s public statements, citing the risk of witness intimidation. This is a dispute about the effect of a defendant’s public speech on court proceedings and the safety of participants, not by itself a finding that each post obstructed justice. The packet does not identify the specific posts, the exact number included in the “dozens” claim, the scope of the restrictions Smith requested or the court’s final rulings. The Washington Post link, which is dated October 5, 2023, timed out during retrieval. Without its article or the relevant court filings, the details of the request and subsequent orders cannot be described. The entry can summarize the reported attacks and prosecutor’s response, but needs the underlying record to support its scale and legal consequences.
subcategory: Attacks on prosecutors, witnesses and judges
notes: Needs context: The Washington Post article timed out. The supplied account does not provide a post list, precise count, the restrictions requested or the court’s final rulings.
Proposed correction: Verify the specific posts and court orders in the full article or filings before presenting the number or legal consequences as established.
Repaired the previously unfinished long description and removed unsupported legal-expert claims from the medium text.

title: Trump threatens to prosecute Biden and Obama on day one (2024)
description_short: NBC reported Trump suggesting he would have Biden indicted if reelected
description_medium: NBC News reported that Donald Trump suggested he would have Joe Biden indicted if reelected, while arguing that he was entitled to immunity for his own official acts. The supplied synopsis adds Obama and a promise to act on “day one,” but the linked article does not establish those details. The remarks describe a conditional threat, not a prosecution that occurred.
description_long: In a January 2024 report, NBC News described Trump suggesting that Joe Biden would be indicted if Trump won another term. The article connected the remark to Trump’s argument that former presidents should receive immunity for official acts and his claim that investigating election fraud had been part of his presidential duties. The supplied synopsis goes further, saying Trump repeatedly promised to prosecute Biden, Barack Obama and other political opponents as retribution on his first day back in office. The linked NBC article’s headline and accessible text support the Biden statement but do not establish an Obama target or a “day one” commitment. The distinction matters: a conditional statement about what Trump might do if elected is not an actual Justice Department prosecution, and the source does not show that any investigation was ordered. A fuller account of the broader rally statements needs a source that documents the alleged Obama reference, timing and retributive purpose. The linked story can support a narrower entry about Trump’s statement concerning Biden and his immunity argument.
subcategory: Conditional threat of prosecution against a political opponent
notes: Needs context: The linked NBC report supports a conditional statement about Biden but not the title’s claim about Obama or a day-one prosecution promise.
Proposed correction: Narrow the title to Trump’s reported Biden-indictment statement unless a separate transcript or report supports the Obama and day-one claims.
Revised the short card text to match the linked report’s narrower account.

title: Pilot Logs Document 11 Epstein Flights Involving Trump
description_short: Pilot Logs Document 11 Epstein Flights Involving Trump
description_medium: The supplied summary says pilot David Rodgers’s logs, introduced in federal proceedings, record at least 11 flights by Donald Trump on aircraft associated with Jeffrey Epstein between 1993 and 1998. The linked Reuters report about a 2025 release of Epstein files returned HTTP 401; the packet does not provide the log pages or verify the routes and count.
description_long: The entry says flight logs maintained by Jeffrey Epstein’s pilot David Rodgers were introduced in federal proceedings and record at least 11 occasions when Donald Trump traveled on aircraft associated with Epstein between 1993 and 1998. The supplied summary lists New York, Atlantic City, Palm Beach and the Virgin Islands as destinations. It also notes that Trump has denied knowing about Epstein’s trafficking activities. Flight records can document travel, but they do not by themselves establish what passengers knew about crimes or whether a flight was connected to trafficking. The summary’s additional claim that Trump-linked social events served as recruitment grounds is not supported by the linked material provided here. Reuters’ article about a December 2025 release of Epstein records returned HTTP 401, and the packet does not include the underlying logs or the specific court exhibit. An accessible copy of the records is needed to confirm the flight count, dates and destinations and to separate the documented travel from unrelated allegations about knowledge or recruitment.
notes: Needs context: The Reuters page returned HTTP 401, and the packet does not include the flight-log exhibit needed to confirm the claimed 11 flights, dates and destinations. The recruitment claim is not supported by the linked source.
Proposed correction: Provide the court exhibit or accessible reporting that identifies the flights, and remove unrelated recruitment claims unless separately sourced.

title: Pre-Inauguration Promises of Jan 6 Pardons
description_medium: The supplied summary says Trump promised pardons for people involved in the January 6 Capitol attack before his January 2025 inauguration and called them “hostages” and “patriots.” Its only linked New York Times article is from August 2023 and concerns the indictment, not the later pardon remarks. The statements need a matching source before their timing and scope can be verified.
description_long: The entry concerns remarks that Donald Trump allegedly made in the days before his January 2025 inauguration about pardoning people charged or convicted in connection with the January 6 Capitol attack. The supplied summary says he called some of them “hostages” and “patriots,” but it provides no dated transcript, count of people covered or specific clemency commitment. Its only linked New York Times article dates to August 2023 and reports on Trump’s indictment; it cannot support remarks made more than a year later. The distinction matters because a public promise before inauguration is separate from the pardons or commutations later issued, and the linked material does not document those outcomes either. The source mismatch prevents a complete account of what Trump said, when he said it or which people he meant. An accessible transcript or contemporaneous report is needed before attributing the quoted labels or describing the promises as a defined clemency policy.
notes: Needs context: The supplied source is an August 2023 indictment story and cannot support the pre-inauguration remarks in January 2025 or subsequent clemency outcomes.
Proposed correction: Replace the linked source with a dated transcript or contemporaneous report and distinguish the pre-inauguration promise from later clemency actions.
Removed unsupported assertions that the remarks themselves rewrote the history of the attack or normalized political violence.

title: Trump Fires 200+ Immigration Judges, Gutting Courts
description_short: Claim about 200+ immigration-judge firings lacks a matching source
description_medium: The supplied description alleges that more than 200 immigration judges were fired in February 2025 and that the change disrupted pending cases. The linked New York Times article is about the dismissal of inspectors general, not immigration judges, so it does not verify the number, affected courts or case outcomes. A matching personnel report is needed.
description_long: The record alleges that the Trump administration fired more than 200 immigration judges in February 2025, along with court staff, and that the dismissals disrupted pending cases. Its linked New York Times article, however, concerns inspectors general who were removed from federal agencies; it does not report on immigration-court personnel. The source therefore cannot support the claimed number of judges, the share of the workforce affected, postponed hearings, alleged civil-service violations or a purpose of enabling deportations without judicial review. Those are material claims that require records of the dismissals and evidence of resulting changes to court schedules and caseloads. The entry can preserve the allegation as a claim in the supplied synopsis, but it should not present it as established fact based on the linked article. An accessible contemporaneous report, personnel notices and immigration-court data are needed to establish who was dismissed, when the actions occurred and what consequences followed.
notes: Needs context: The linked Times report concerns inspectors general, not immigration judges, and does not substantiate the asserted judge count, case impacts or motive.
Proposed correction: Obtain a contemporaneous report or DOJ personnel and caseload records before retaining the firing count and consequences.
Replaced the unsupported populated medium and short-card text with an attributed allegation and source mismatch.
